findings.claim: Bookings with a Google Meet location crash with a TypeError when no destination calendar is set. Before the patch they fell back to Cal Video.
findings.evidence: Line 118 is `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, which yields undefined. Line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no `?.`; the base had `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 passes null in this case, and the confirm and payment webhook callers pass []. Three seats ran a standalone node one-liner that mirrors this expression and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. That one-liner does not import project code.
findings.reason: Main list: four seats. Ponytail raised it as out of remit and passed it on. Red test before fixing: call `EventManager.create` with location MeetLocationType and destinationCalendar null or [].

verifier.reason: packages/core/EventManager.ts:118 gives `mainHostDestinationCalendar` the value undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or [], and handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 passes null when no calendar is set. Line 119 then reads `.integration` without `?.` whenever the location is Google Meet, so it throws a TypeError where the old `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` fell back to Cal Video.

findings.claim: The organization slug condition is inverted, in a change unrelated to the PR. With billing off (self-hosted), orgs are created with no slug. With billing on, they get the slug before payment.
findings.evidence: The base had `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`; the head has `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Line 153 (requestedSlug) is unchanged in meaning. With billing off, createTeams.handler.ts:66-67 then throws NoOrganizationSlugError. The open-code-review node one-liner shows the two expressions give opposite results for each value of IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED. The change came in with commit db92960dc4.
findings.reason: Main list: four seats. Ponytail raised it as out of remit and as churn. Red test before fixing: an org-create test with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false that asserts the slug is set.

verifier.reason: The patch changes create.handler.ts:151 from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, so the condition is now inverted. With billing off, the org gets neither a slug nor a requestedSlug (line 153), so createTeams.handler.ts:67-68 throws NoOrganizationSlugError. With billing on, the slug is set before payment.

findings.claim: The collective fix does nothing when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, so the other hosts' calendars are silently dropped.
findings.evidence: Lines 1063-1067 set evt.destinationCalendar to null in that case. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, and createAllCalendarEvents takes the organizer-only legacy branch at EventManager.ts:384+. mattpocock also notes that the confirm and payment handlers only ever wrap the organizer's calendar, which leaves the same gap after confirmation or payment (unverified). Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Main list: four seats. Red test before fixing: a COLLECTIVE booking where the organizer has no destination calendar and a second host has one should create an event for that host.

verifier.reason: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets evt.destinationCalendar to null, so the optional-chained push of teamDestinationCalendars at handleNewBooking.ts:1078 does nothing. createAllCalendarEvents then falls to the else branch at EventManager.ts:384-396, which writes only to the organizer's first connected calendar, so the other hosts' calendars are silently dropped.

findings.claim: The fallback calendar ID in updateEvent (line 256) and deleteEvent (line 317) is dead code, so the old fallback to the destination calendar's externalId is lost.
findings.evidence: The code is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. The find only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it can never match. As a result, update sends `calendarId: undefined`, which fails. Delete falls back to "primary", and its 404 is swallowed. The base used destinationCalendar.externalId. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Main list: four seats. Red test before fixing: update or delete a reference with a null externalCalendarId and assert that the destination calendar's externalId is used. Ponytail's suggested restore is `externalCalendarId || mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`.

verifier.reason: At CalendarService.ts:254-256 and 315-317, the `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it cannot return a real calendar ID (it could only match an empty or null externalId). The old fallback to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId` is gone, so updateEvent sends `calendarId: undefined` and deleteEvent falls back to "primary", where a 404 is resolved silently (line 335).

findings.claim: When cancelling a recurring booking, the series-delete block runs once per calendar reference. It always uses the organizer's credentials and only the first calendar reference. This causes N duplicate deletes, and other hosts' copies are never deleted.
findings.evidence: The recurring block now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` but does not depend on reference. It loops over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and uses `.find` for the first `_calendar` reference. The seats cite different line ranges for the same block: 423-466 (mattpocock), 443-469 (ponytail), 422-482 (superpowers) and 620-659 (open-code-review). Reasoned.
findings.reason: Main list: four seats. Severity normalised to Important; ponytail rated it Minor. Red test before fixing: cancel a recurring collective booking with two host references and assert one delete per host event.

verifier.reason: At handleCancelBooking.ts:449-461 the recurring branch sits inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop (line 423), but it never uses `reference`. It loops over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, the organizer's, and calls `.find` to take only the first `_calendar` ref of each updated booking (line 454). So it repeats the same deletes once per reference, and other hosts' copies of the series are never deleted.

coverage: Gate not run (benchmark mode): no build, typecheck, unit tests, e2e tests or lint. The review is unanchored, and every finding is reasoned from source. The only runtime evidence is standalone node one-liners (Meet crash, slug inversion) that mirror the logic without importing project code. No spec: all seats inferred the intent (every COLLECTIVE host's destination calendar gets the event on create, reschedule and cancel) from issue #7754, the branch name and commit messages. Standards sources: only CONTRIBUTING.md, .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md and packages/config/eslint-preset.js. There is no AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or .cursorrules. mattpocock skipped lint rules as tool-enforced, and open-code-review applied only its generic TS/JS checklist. Every seat reports reading all 22 files, but with these limits. mattpocock read builder.ts, larkcalendar, office365calendar and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts diff-only and did not trace callers; it checked the payment and booking handlers (webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, bookingReminder.ts, confirm, editLocation, requestReschedule, deleteCredential) only for array wrapping. superpowers treated builder.ts, class.ts, Calendar.d.ts and EventManager.d.ts as type-only, and read bookingReminder.ts, webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, deleteCredential, confirm, editLocation, requestReschedule and BrokenIntegrationEmail.tsx diff-only; it did not check every Calendar implementer against the new createEvent signature. ponytail did not confirm whether dropping the organization select breaks a downstream reader. All seats are from one model family; no cross-family correctness seat ran. Rejections: none. No finding was disproven by the seat reports, so the verifier path was not needed.
